: Module overview {.striped}

The module is an elective in the handbooks of M.Sc. VWL and M.Sc. BWL (PNPM).

## Prerequisites

Mathematics, statistics, probability theory, and regression analysis (estimation
and hypothesis testing). Python is essential for the exercise sessions.

## Content

The module covers the fundamentals of Bayesian inference and their application to
high-dimensional datasets in economics and finance, with equal weight on
theoretical foundations and empirical implementation in Python.

- Subjective probability and the Bayesian paradigm
- MCMC algorithms: Gibbs sampling and Metropolis-Hastings
- Shrinkage and the Minnesota prior
- BVARs and state-space models for macroeconomics
- Stochastic volatility and portfolio choice
- Bayesian machine learning for causal inference

## Learning outcomes

After completing the module, students are able to

- explain the theoretical foundations of Bayesian inference and subjective probability,
- analyse complex, high-dimensional datasets with modern Bayesian techniques,
- apply Bayesian econometric methods to empirical problems in economics and finance,
- implement standard Bayesian algorithms and models in original Python code,
- critically evaluate empirical findings while accounting for uncertainty.

## Assessment and reading

The module is assessed by a 90-minute written exam, see [Assessment](assessment.qmd).
The reading list is on the [Literature](literature.qmd) page. Course material and
updates are distributed via ILIAS.
